Thanksgiving 2026

Four recipes for Thanksgiving: slow-cooked turkey, maple-roasted squash, a savory tart, and something fresh.

November 26, 20262 mains · 2 sides

Main

Slow-cooker turkey breast with lemon-garlic gravy

An overnight herb brine, a slow cooker, and a short turn under the broiler. Serve with a lemony gravy made from the cooking juices.

Serves
5–7
Prep
10 min
Dry brine
8–12 hr
Slow cook
4–6 hr

Ingredients

Turkey

  • 1½ tbsp coarse kosher salt
  • 1½ tbsp dried thyme
  • 1½ tbsp dried rosemary
  • 1 tbsp onion powder
  • 1 tbsp sweet paprika
  • 1 tbsp packed light brown sugar
  • Freshly ground black pepper
  • 1 whole bone-in, skin-on turkey breast (5–7 lb)
  • 2 carrots, scrubbed; no need to peel or cut
  • 1 large yellow or red onion, sliced into 3 or 4 thick rings
  • 1 large head garlic, halved crosswise
  • 4 tbsp unsalted butter, softened

Gravy

  • Chicken or turkey broth or stock, if needed
  • 1 tbsp unsalted butter
  • 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
  • Juice of 1 lemon
  • Freshly ground black pepper

Method

  1. Dry-brine overnightCombine the salt, thyme, rosemary, onion powder, paprika, brown sugar, and several generous grinds of black pepper in a small bowl. Pat the turkey breast dry and put it in a very large bowl. Remove and discard the pop-up thermometer, if present. Coat all over with the salt mixture, including the bone and under the skin. Gently loosen the skin with your fingers to season the meat underneath. Arrange skin-side up and refrigerate uncovered for 8–12 hours.
  2. Slow-cookRemove the turkey from the refrigerator about 1 hour before cooking. Put the carrots, onion, and garlic in the bottom of a 6–8-quart slow cooker; it is fine if the garlic falls apart. Set the turkey on top, skin-side up. Smear the softened butter under the skin. Cook on low until the thickest part just registers 155°F on an instant-read thermometer, about 4–6 hours. Start checking at about 3 hours 45 minutes to gauge how quickly it is cooking.
  3. TransferUsing tongs, lift the turkey onto a sheet pan. If it is done much sooner than you are ready to eat, tent it with foil and let it sit at room temperature before proceeding.
  4. Brown the skinPosition an oven rack about 8 inches from the broiler heat source, farther away than usual, and turn the broiler to high. Broil for 6–9 minutes total, checking and rotating the turkey every 3 minutes, until the skin is browned and crisp.
  5. RestLet the turkey rest for at least 10 minutes.
  6. Collect the drippingsMeanwhile, remove and discard the onion and carrots from the slow cooker. Squeeze the soft garlic out of its papery skins into the drippings; discard the skins. Pour the drippings and garlic into a liquid measuring cup. Add broth or stock if needed to make 2 cups.
  7. Make the gravyMelt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the flour and whisk into evenly moistened, sizzling crumbles. Pour in the 2 cups of drippings and simmer, whisking, until thick enough to coat a spoon, about 3 minutes. Add the lemon juice and smash the garlic with a fork. Season with black pepper. For a smooth gravy, strain through a fine sieve.
  8. ServeCarve the turkey breast and serve with the warm gravy.

Notes

Before you begin. Use a 6–8-quart slow cooker. A breast larger than about 6½ lb may not fit a 6-quart model. If frozen, allow a day or two to thaw completely in the refrigerator; do not put frozen meat in the slow cooker.

Temperature in the original recipe. The author specifies a 155°F pull temperature, followed by broiling and resting, and explains that the long cooking time and carryover heat are part of this method. That temperature and sequence are preserved here.

For 2–4 people. Use a 2–3½ lb half turkey breast, preferably bone-in and skin-on; boneless, skinless also works, though the author considers skin more important than bone. For the brine, use 1½–2 tsp coarse kosher salt (the smaller amount for under 3 lb), 2 tsp each dried thyme, dried rosemary, onion powder, and paprika, 1½ tsp light brown sugar, and several grinds of pepper. Use the same aromatics, but only 2 tbsp softened butter under the skin. Cook on low for 2½–3½ hours; start checking at 2 hours 15 minutes. Follow the same broiling and resting steps. Make the gravy with 1 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp flour, 1 cup drippings/broth, and the juice of ½ lemon.

Source: Sarah DiGregorio · NYT Cooking · November 4, 2024.

Main

Stuffed butternut squash

Maple-roasted squash with bacon, sunchokes, long beans, and sage; finished with caramelized onions and toasted walnuts.

Serves
4
Roast
About 45 min
Finish
10–15 min
Total
About 1½ hr

Ingredients

Squash & topping

  • 2 medium butternut squashes
  • 2 tbsp olive oil, divided
  • 4 tbsp maple syrup, divided
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • 1 large onion; half thinly sliced, half diced
  • ½ cup chopped walnuts
  • 1 tbsp walnut oil
  • Chopped fresh parsley, to finish

Filling

  • 4 slices bacon, diced (about 4 oz)
  • 8 oz sunchokes, scrubbed and finely diced
  • 6 oz long beans, trimmed and sliced into short pieces
  • Finely grated zest of 1 lemon
  • 2 tbsp chopped fresh sage
  • 1 tsp fennel seeds, lightly crushed
  • 1 tbsp dried parsley
  • 1 tsp dried thyme
  • ¼ cup grated cheddar
  • ¼ cup grated Parmesan
  • ½ cup breadcrumbs
  • 2 tbsp lemon juice

Method

  1. Roast the squashHeat the oven to 375°F. Halve the squashes lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Put cut-side up on a baking sheet. Brush the cut surfaces with 1 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp maple syrup, then season with salt and pepper. Roast for about 45 minutes, until the flesh is fork-tender; larger squash may need longer.
  2. Caramelize the sliced onionMeanwhile, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add the sliced half of the onion and a pinch of salt. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden and soft, about 25–35 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and keep the skillet for the walnuts.
  3. Cook the fillingIn a second skillet, cook the bacon over medium heat until it starts to release its fat. Add the diced onion and sunchokes. Cook, stirring, until the sunchokes are nearly tender. Add the long beans and lemon zest, then sauté until all the vegetables are tender. Stir in the sage, fennel, dried parsley, and thyme and cook briefly, just until fragrant.
  4. Chop & toastPulse the filling briefly in a food processor, leaving a coarse texture. Do not purée it. Toast the chopped walnuts in the emptied onion skillet over medium-low heat, stirring, until fragrant. Set the walnuts aside.
  5. Mix the fillingCombine the chopped filling, cheddar, Parmesan, breadcrumbs, lemon juice, and 1 tbsp maple syrup. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper.
  6. Fill & finishSpoon the filling into the squash cavities and mound any extra over the cut flesh. Top with the caramelized onions. Lightly brush the exposed long necks of the squash with the walnut oil and remaining 1 tbsp maple syrup, then press the toasted walnuts onto the glazed surfaces. Return to the oven for 10–15 minutes, until the filling is hot and the cheese has melted.
  7. ServeSprinkle with fresh parsley and serve warm.

Notes

Kitchen note. The original handwritten recipe did not specify every quantity. The amounts above are suggested for 2 medium squashes; the ½ cup of grated cheese is split equally between cheddar and Parmesan. The brief final bake is an added finishing step.

Source: Eric’s kitchen notes · November 2024.

Side

Caramelized carrot tarte Tatin with ginger

Roasted carrots, an orange-ginger glaze, and crisp puff pastry, turned out and finished with dill, hazelnuts, and feta.

Serves
6–8
Active
50 min
Total
2 hr
Skillet
12 inches

Ingredients

  • 2 lb small carrots (about 6 inches long), peeled and halved lengthwise
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • ¾ tsp ground cumin
  • 1½ tsp kosher salt, divided
  • ½ tsp black pepper, divided
  • 1 piece fresh ginger (4 inches), peeled
  • ¼ cup fresh orange juice
  • 3 tbsp granulated sugar
  • 3 tbsp white balsamic vinegar
  • 3 tbsp unsalted butter
  • ¾ tsp fish sauce
  • 1 package frozen puff pastry (14 oz, such as Dufour), thawed
  • Fresh dill, chopped toasted hazelnuts, and crumbled feta, for garnish

Method

  1. Roast the carrotsPreheat the oven to 425°F. Toss the carrots, oil, cumin, 1 tsp salt, and ¼ tsp pepper on a large rimmed baking sheet until evenly coated. Arrange in a single layer, cut-sides down, and roast until tender, 25–30 minutes. Set aside; leave the oven on.
  2. Press the gingerMeanwhile, finely grate the ginger with a Microplane. Put it in a fine wire-mesh strainer over a small bowl. Stir and press to extract about 2 tbsp ginger juice; discard the solids.
  3. Make the glazeWhisk the ginger juice, orange juice, sugar, vinegar, remaining ½ tsp salt, and remaining ¼ tsp pepper in a 12-inch stainless steel skillet. Cook over medium-low heat, swirling occasionally, until reduced to a thick syrup that just coats the bottom, 7–10 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the butter and fish sauce. Set aside.
  4. Prepare the pastryOn a lightly floured surface, roll the puff pastry to a 14 × 12-inch rectangle. Use a pot lid or plate as a guide to cut a 12-inch circle; discard the scraps. Transfer the round to a parchment-lined baking sheet. Score it all over with ½-inch-long slits. Cover with a second sheet of parchment and refrigerate until ready to use.
  5. AssembleArrange the carrots cut-sides down, tightly packed in an even layer, in the glaze in the skillet. Place the chilled pastry round over the carrots, folding the edges inward as needed to fit inside the skillet.
  6. Bake & invertBake at 425°F until the pastry is puffed and golden, about 20 minutes. With the tart still in the oven, reduce the temperature to 375°F and bake until deeply browned, 15–20 minutes more. Let cool in the skillet for 5 minutes. Loosen the pastry edges with an offset spatula if needed. Set a wire rack inside a rimmed baking sheet and carefully invert the tart onto it. Let cool until no longer steaming, about 15 minutes.
  7. FinishTransfer to a serving plate or cutting board. Garnish with dill, hazelnuts, and feta. Slice and serve warm or at room temperature.

Notes

Ginger juice. Store-bought bottled ginger juice can replace freshly pressed ginger juice. Do not use ginger syrup, which is too sweet. The original note suggests specialty grocery stores or itsthejuice.com.

From the magazine. The suggested wine pairing is a fruit-forward, citrusy sparkling wine, such as NV Nino Franco Rustico Prosecco. Photo styling: Margaret Dickey; prop styling: Christina Daley.

Source: Nicole Hopper · Food & Wine · March 2025, pp. 44–45.

Side

Sunshine salad with carrot-ginger dressing

Smashed cucumbers, avocado, red onion, and Thai basil over a bright carrot-ginger dressing, with toasted sesame to finish.

Serves
4 as a side
Prep
10 min
Salting
30 min

Ingredients

Salad

  • 1 lb 10 oz (750 g) Lebanese or Persian cucumbers
  • ½ red onion, peeled and thinly sliced into rounds (½ cup / 60 g)
  • 1 tbsp lime juice
  • ¼ cup (5 g) Thai basil leaves
  • 1 large ripe avocado, peeled, halved, pitted, and thinly sliced at an angle
  • 2 tsp sesame seeds, well toasted
  • 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
  • Salt

Carrot-ginger dressing

  • 2–3 carrots (9 oz / 250 g), peeled and roughly chopped into ¾-inch (2 cm) pieces
  • ¾ oz (20 g) fresh ginger, peeled and roughly chopped
  • 1 tbsp honey
  • 1 tbsp soy sauce
  • 1½ tbsp white miso
  • 2 tbsp rice vinegar
  • 2 tbsp lime juice
  • 5 tbsp (75 ml) olive oil
  • ¼ cup (60 ml) water

Method

  1. Salt the cucumbersUse the flat side of a knife to bash each cucumber along its length a few times, until it starts to break in places. Halve lengthwise and remove and discard the seedy insides. Slice at an angle into ¾–1-inch (2–2½ cm) pieces. Put in a bowl with ¾ tsp salt, toss, and let rest for 30 minutes to draw out as much water as possible. Drain in a sieve, discarding the salty water. Return the cucumbers to the bowl and gently toss with the onion, lime juice, and basil.
  2. Blend the dressingMeanwhile, put all the dressing ingredients in a food processor or blender with ¼ tsp salt. Blend until completely smooth; this may take a few minutes. Strain through a sieve over a bowl, pushing to extract as much dressing as possible. Save the pulp for another use.
  3. Season the avocadoSprinkle the sliced avocado with a pinch of salt.
  4. AssemblePour the dressing onto a large, lipped plate, swirling to coat the base. Top with half the avocado, then all the cucumber mixture, then the remaining avocado. Finish with the sesame seeds and sesame oil. Serve straight away.

Notes

Keep the extra dressing. Refrigerate in a sterilized jar for up to 3 days. Whisk together again before using, as the liquid and solids naturally separate. Try it with crunchy green leaves such as iceberg or little gem lettuce, or thinly shredded red and white cabbage.

Texture. The cookbook introduction allows leaving the dressing unstrained if you prefer; straining gives the smoothest result.

Source: Noor Murad & Yotam Ottolenghi · Ottolenghi Test Kitchen: Extra Good Things · p. 150.
